description: Calculate thermal resistance (R-value and U-value) for composite walls with multiple layers.

seo.title: Thermal Resistance Calculator - R-Value U-Value
seo.description: Calculate thermal resistance (R-value) and overall U-value for composite wall, roof, or floor assemblies with multiple material layers.

formula.explanation: U = 1/R_total. R_total = R_inside + Σ(L_i/k_i) + R_outside. Three material layers provided: L in m, k in W/mK. h in W/m²K.

content.introduction: Calculate the overall heat transfer coefficient (U-value) for a composite wall assembly with up to 3 material layers plus convection resistances on both sides. U-value is the reciprocal of total R-value.

example.description: 100mm brick + 50mm insulation + 10mm plasterboard: U ≈ 0.62 W/m²K (well-insulated wall).

faq.q: What is the difference between R-value and U-value?
faq.a: R is thermal resistance (m²K/W) — higher is better insulation. U is heat transfer coefficient (W/m²K) — lower is better. U = 1/R_total.
Modern insulated walls: 0.2-0.4 W/m²K; roofs: 0.15-0.25; windows: 1.5-3.0; uninsulated solid brick: 2.0-3.0.
